hens_rule_text: Hen limit scales with lot size: 2 hens on lots up to about 5,009 sq ft (0.11 acre), rising to as many as 6 on larger residential lots. A Metro permit is required regardless of flock size.
permit_notes: A Domestic Hen Permit from Metro Public Health / Animal Care and Control is required, renewed periodically, with a signed rules-and-regulations form.
setback_notes: Hen house and enclosure must be in the side or rear yard, never the front yard, and at least 25 ft from a neighboring residence.
coop_rules: Hen house must be fully enclosed with a roof, lockable doors, and predator-proof screening on any openings (holes smaller than one square inch); it must provide at least 2 sq ft per hen, with the outdoor fenced run providing at least 6 sq ft per hen; the area must be kept free of trash and accumulated droppings.
zoning_notes: Rules apply to residential lots citywide under Metro's domestic hen permitting program, administered by Animal Care and Control; the state has no law overriding local rules (a 2024 bill to protect up to six hens statewide did not pass, per Tennessee's state-law entry).
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Nashville.gov, Get or Renew Domestic Hen Permit
